newsitem.title: USA: CME lauds Taiwan offshore stock futures ban lift.
newsitem.headline: CME lauds Taiwan offshore stock futures ban lift.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange lauded Taiwan's decision Wednesday to lift in April its ban on local trading of offshore Taiwan stock-index futures contracts.

"This development...will enable market forces, and not insular regulations, to determine what Taiwanese stock index products will be successful in global markets," CME chairman Jack Sandner said Friday in a memo to members. "We commend the decision of the Finance Minister to open the Taiwanese futures market to this degree and welcome the opportunity it will give the Merc to compete on a more level field."

Taiwan's finance minister Paul Chiu announced the liberalization March 5, saying the Taiwan Stock Exchange will launch stock warrants in April before offshore stock-index futures are approved but both should be approved in April.
The decision means Taiwan futures firms for the first time will be able to trade CME and Singapore International Monetary Market futures that are linked to Taiwan stock market moves.

CME's Dow Jones Taiwan Stock Index futures started January 9. But under a Taiwan Futures Trading Law enacted Tuesday, a planned futures exchange in Taipei can open no sooner than October, months after the CME and SIMEX products began. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
